thread:
Jonas Weber: now that v1 is live, we should lock a plan for (a) next refresh date and (b) what counts as a “material change” where we need to republish PDF / update claims vs just update the interactive table. don’t want this to be vibes-based.

Claire Dubois: +1. also we need to define “refresh” separately for: dataset (prompt set), methodology/config, runtime/software version, pricing inputs.

Rina Kobayashi: fwiw the harness is ready to rerun in ~2-3 days if we reserve fleet. but scheduling needs to account for region sweep queue + stability gates.

Nadia Rahman: and pricing/latency/$ can move even if perf doesn’t. if token price changes, latency/$ shifts. we need to decide if we freeze $ inputs for the report period or always use current list pricing.

Henry Cho: product angle: the interactive page can be “live” and show “Last updated: <date>” + changelog. the PDF is the thing sales/legal will treat as a fixed artifact.

Mei Lin: can we align on a cadence proposal? my vote: quarterly full refresh (PDF + dataset) + monthly “table-only” refresh if we have meaningful runtime improvements.

Jonas Weber: seems reasonable. but the big question is: what’s “meaningful” / “material”.

Claire Dubois: rough idea:
- material = anything that would change the takeaway / headline claims or invalidate previous comparisons
- non-material = routine variance within our confidence bands / minor bugfixes that don’t change numbers beyond threshold

Rina Kobayashi: we can quantify threshold as “if median latency/$ or p95 latency changes by > X% for any published model+region cell”. pick X. 5%? 10%?

Nadia Rahman: for latency/$, 5% can happen from noise in smaller regions unless we increase repeats. i’d prefer:
- material if >10% change in latency/$ for ≥3 of the top-viewed cells (top models/regions) OR >15% for any single cell
- plus a special case: any change that impacts the top-3 ranking table we show on the landing page

Mei Lin: we can drive this from analytics: “top-viewed cells” = cells that make up 80% of table impressions. (Felix can pull that but we can approximate now: llama / mistral / qwen + us-east, us-west, eu-west)

Henry Cho: also “material” should include introducing/removing a region from “supported” list, since the narrative talks about regional consistency.

Elliot Price: from docs POV: we need a crisp list we can put into the methodology page + internal process. something like “we will republish when: methodology changes, model list changes, hardware class changes, pricing inputs change, or results move beyond threshold”.

Soojin Lee: + a note for PMM: if we republish PDF we need a mini-launch process (legal re-approval, sales enablement update, etc). so we should keep that bar relatively high.

Jonas Weber: ok let’s enumerate candidates:
1) new model added / model removed
2) model version change (e.g., upstream weights revision) or tokenizer change
3) hardware type change in a region (H100 -> B200, etc)
4) runtime major version change (kernels/batching policy changes)
5) methodology changes (prompt set, concurrency, caching policy)
6) region list changes (new region, deprecate region)
7) pricing changes used in latency/$
8) bug fix in measurement pipeline

Claire Dubois: agree. but (4) “runtime major version” is tricky: we deploy continuously. we need a line like “any runtime change that materially affects published metrics beyond thresholds”.

Rina Kobayashi: we already capture runner image digest + runtime commit in the manifest. so we can detect “new runtime commit” but not every commit should trigger a PDF.

Nadia Rahman: (7) pricing: I strongly recommend the PDF uses list pricing as-of a “pricing snapshot date” and doesn’t auto-update. interactive page can optionally show current pricing. otherwise you can’t reproduce an old latency/$ value if pricing changed.

Henry Cho: +1. legal will also like “as of <date>”.

Soojin Lee: yes, we can message “Benchmarks captured June 2025; pricing as of June X, 2025.” and then the interactive page has a toggle: “pricing basis: at run date / current” (if we can do it). but PDF needs to freeze.

Mei Lin: we need a changelog artifact regardless. even if not material, we should log “table updated; no methodology change; results within expected variance”.

Jonas Weber: so proposal:
- Full refresh cadence: quarterly (Q3, Q4, etc)
- Table-only refresh cadence: monthly, but only if stability gates pass and we have capacity
- Material change triggers PDF republish + methodology page update + legal signoff

Claire Dubois: define material change triggers as:
A) Any change to methodology inputs: prompt set version, concurrency profile, warmup/stability settings, caching/batching policy
B) Any change to model catalog in the report (add/remove) OR model revision
C) Any change to “supported regions” list used in report
D) Any change to pricing snapshot basis (or pricing itself) that shifts latency/$ beyond threshold
E) Any metric shift beyond threshold (say >15% any single cell OR >10% across multiple high-traffic cells) after controlling for noise (repeat runs)
F) Any bug that affects published numbers outside threshold

Rina Kobayashi: we should add a “re-run required” step before concluding it’s material. e.g., if a cell shifts > threshold, rerun 2x; if persists, mark as real.

Mei Lin: +1. otherwise we’ll chase flakes.

Jonas Weber: what about “new runtime release that improves things materially”? do we want to republish quickly as a “v1.1” or just let table update + mention in changelog?

Soojin Lee: PMM preference: unless it changes our headline claim or competitiveness story, table update + changelog is enough. republishing PDF frequently will create confusion in the field.

Henry Cho: product note: the landing page currently references “Download the report (PDF)”. if the table is “newer” than the PDF, we must avoid mismatch that looks like bait-and-switch. so we should keep “table results updated <date>; PDF reflects results as-of <date>” super explicit.

Elliot Price: docs can add a banner on the interactive page: “PDF report uses benchmark snapshot v1.0 (June 2025). Interactive table may include newer runs. See changelog.”

Nadia Rahman: also: any change that moves “latency/$” ranking order in the hero chart should be treated as material for marketing. that’s basically what users will screenshot.

Claire Dubois: agree, but we need something deterministic. can define “hero chart set” explicitly: {top 5 models} x {us-east, eu-west} for context len bucket 8k, concurrency profile default.

Jonas Weber: ok let’s do:
- “Hero slice” = the exact slice used in the report’s main chart(s). if any of those cells move >10% and the order changes, it’s material.

Rina Kobayashi: I can wire a check in the pipeline: compare new snapshot vs published snapshot, compute deltas for hero slice + overall, and output “material_change_candidate: true/false” in the validation report.

Mei Lin: + i can store that in the dataset master sheet / validation status.

Soojin Lee: can we loop legal on the definition? we need a written internal policy so sales isn’t accidentally quoting “live numbers” while holding an older PDF.

Michael Grant: jumping in (saw the @mention). general guidance: having a clear “snapshot date” and a defined republish threshold is good. “material” from a claims standpoint is anything that would make a reasonable reader’s interpretation different.
- If you change methodology or inputs, treat as material.
- If you update numbers without republishing the PDF, you must clearly label that the PDF is a historical snapshot and the interactive table is updated independently.
- If you make comparative claims (even implied via rankings), any update that changes the basis of the comparison should go through the same review path.

Jonas Weber: thanks. we’ll write this up.

Claire Dubois: scheduling: when do we want the next run window? given launch traffic, maybe we wait 3-4 weeks to avoid stepping on other fleet needs.

Rina Kobayashi: earliest I can get clean sweeps with capacity is week of July 7 (Vanessa said eu-west is tight next 2 weeks). if we do table-only refresh, we can pick 2 regions + hero slice only, not full matrix.

Mei Lin: +1. “hero refresh” is cheaper and still validates whether runtime/pricing drift is changing the story.

Nadia Rahman: for a July hero refresh, we should keep pricing frozen (still June snapshot) and only update perf metrics. then later quarterly refresh can update pricing snapshot.

Henry Cho: sounds like:
- July: hero slice refresh (table-only) + changelog entry
- Sept: full quarterly refresh + new PDF if needed

Soojin Lee: ok with that. PMM can message internally: “next planned refresh: early July (interactive only), next report update: Sept (quarterly)”.

Jonas Weber: action items:
- Jonas/Claire: draft “material change / republish policy” (1 pager) + post in #eng-ml and send to Soojin/Michael
- Rina: add pipeline diff check for hero slice + thresholds; output flag
- Mei: add changelog tab + analytics-based “top cells” definition
- Nadia: propose pricing snapshot handling for latency/$ (PDF vs table)

Claire Dubois: :thumbsup: I’ll start a draft with explicit threshold numbers and rerun requirement.

Rina Kobayashi: :thumbsup: will prototype the diff check today. need the published snapshot ID (v1.0) pinned somewhere.

Mei Lin: :thumbsup: i’ll pull current page analytics from Logan/Felix and suggest the “top-viewed” set.

Michael Grant: pls include the disclaimer language you intend to use for “interactive table updates” in the draft. that’s the part that usually gets people into trouble.

Soojin Lee: noted. i’ll add to the PMM checklist + make sure Sales enablement doc points to the changelog.

Jonas Weber: great. let’s aim to finalize policy by EOW so we don’t drift.
